title: Median and PERCENTILE_CONT
description: Compute a correct median per group and explain how PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates.

data.text: You need the median salary per department. The table has millions of rows, so you cannot sort in the app. Someone suggested `PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)`, someone else an `AVG` over the middle rows. Write the query and explain when the two disagree.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- Standard approach: an interpolated median.
-- With an odd count, PERCENTILE_CONT returns the exact middle value.
-- With an even count, it returns the average of the two middle values.
SELECT DISTINCT
    Department,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Salary)
        OVER (PARTITION BY Department) AS MedianSalary
FROM Employees;

-- Equivalent hand-rolled median using row numbers (works anywhere).
WITH Ranked AS
(
    SELECT
        Department,
        Salary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Department ORDER BY Salary) AS rn,
        COUNT(*)    OVER (PARTITION BY Department)                  AS cnt
    FROM Employees
)
SELECT
    Department,
    AVG(Salary) AS MedianSalary
FROM Ranked
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)   -- middle one or two rows
GROUP BY Department;

-- Discrete alternative: returns an actual salary that exists in the data.
SELECT DISTINCT
    Department,
    PERCENTILE_DISC(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Salary)
        OVER (PARTITION BY Department) AS MedianSalaryDiscrete
FROM Employees;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: `PERCENTILE_CONT` **interpolates**, so with an even number of rows the median is the mean of the two middle values — a number that may not exist in the table. For an odd count both approaches return the exact middle row. `PERCENTILE_DISC` instead returns the smallest value in the data whose cumulative distribution reaches the percentile, so the result is always a real row. Because `PERCENTILE_CONT` is a window function you must wrap it in `SELECT DISTINCT` or a subquery to get one row per group. On very large tables, a single `PERCENTILE_CONT` over millions of rows can be expensive; for an approximate median, an index seek on the middle row number (via `OFFSET` over an ordered index) is often dramatically cheaper.
